Behavior & Comms Score 3.0: Definitive Overhaul Blueprint
The current Behavior & Communication Score system often punishes innocent players while letting actual griefers slide. Here is a comprehensive blueprint to completely rework the system and make matchmaking fair again

If anyone at VALVE is reading this to rework the behavior & communication score algorithm — you need to integrate a baseline text-verification filter & automated audio transcription before letting raw report volume tank a user's score. Free consulting


1. Overwatch Clean-Up & Quality Control

Elite Patrol Only: Access to Overwatch adjudication must be strictly locked to players who maintain a 12,000 Behavior Score and fall into high-MMR brackets

Honey-Pot / Dummy Cases: The system must regularly feed reviewers control test cases with obvious answers (e.g., clear griefing or clear innocence). Failing these control tests results in an immediate, permanent revocation of Overwatch access


2. Performance Shield (Protection for Carrying and Supporting)

Metric-Based Protection: If a player maintains a solid KDA, high Hero Damage, competitive Net Worth, or high overall combat impact, all Griefing reports against them should be automatically blocked by the system. For support roles, this shield must also trigger based on high healing, camps stacked, or high warding impact. A player must not be punished for an unusual item build or a non-meta pick if their performance metrics prove they were actively fighting and creating space

Exception: This performance shield only drops if Overwatch manually reviews the case and proves the player was actively ignoring the main objectives or throwing the game despite having good individual stats

Furthermore, if game telemetry detects absolutely no signs of abandoning, intentional feeding, griefing, or AFK behavior, the player must receive a guaranteed, flat increase to their behavior score after the match. Unverified or false reports from salty teammates must be completely ignored by this calculation and must never block the score increase


3. Fair Report Filtering & Automation Control

Griefing Logs Verification: The system should only accept Griefing reports if game telemetry registers specific automated flags: item destruction, mass item selling, shadow amulet (example) abuse, or system-detected strict AFK status

Mute Protection: If a player remains completely silent or has incoming/outgoing chat disabled, all Communication Abuse against them must be instantly discarded

Anti-Bullying Mitigation: Multiple reports from the same party must count as exactly ONE report. Furthermore, if a user spams reports in every single match, their report weight should drop to zero, rendering their votes ignored

Non-Automated Reports Logic: All other reports — such as Role Abuse, Ability Abuse, or Cheating — must never be automated. They should be routed strictly to Overwatch, ensuring real high-MMR players manually review the incidents

Technical Note on Voice Communications & Infrastructure:

To anyone wondering how a text filter would handle voice chat: the technology already exists and is actively used by competitors. Riot Games uses an integrated pipeline (like in Valorant and League of Legends) where a voice report triggers an automated Speech-to-Text tool. The audio is transcribed into text data and fed directly into the same NLP model to verify toxicity before any penalty is applied

The technology is not the issue here; it’s strictly a question of server infrastructure and operational costs. Riot reinvests into processing layers (Speech-to-Text pipelines), while VALVE cuts costs by optimizing purely for raw telemetry data volume. VALVE chooses not to compute voice data, leaving Dota's 2 system completely blind to the actual context of your audio. If we want a true Behavior & Comms 3.0, VALVE needs to stop cutting corners on server-side moderation
